Package com.nexuslink.ui.files

Class FileBrowserPane

java.lang.Object
javafx.scene.Node
javafx.scene.Parent
javafx.scene.layout.Region
javafx.scene.layout.Pane
javafx.scene.layout.VBox
com.nexuslink.ui.files.FileBrowserPane
All Implemented Interfaces:
javafx.css.Styleable, javafx.event.EventTarget
public final class FileBrowserPane extends javafx.scene.layout.VBox
One pane of the DualPaneBrowser: an address bar, a navigation toolbar (Up / Refresh / New Folder) and a details table (name · size · modified · permissions) over a FileSystem. Double-clicking a directory navigates into it; double-clicking a file fires setOnActivateFile(java.util.function.Consumer<com.nexuslink.ui.files.FileItem>). All blocking I/O runs on a background thread so the UI never freezes — the WinSCP/MobaXterm feel.

    • setOnSameSideMove

      public void setOnSameSideMove(BiConsumer<List<FileItem>,String> handler)
      Notified when entries dragged from this pane are dropped onto one of its own folder rows: the items and the target folder. Such a move stays on one file system, so the container performs it as a rename rather than a copy-and-delete (see SameSideMove).

    • loadStartDir

      public void loadStartDir(String preferred)
      Loads preferred if it still lists, else the file system's home. Use for a directory remembered from an earlier session: it may since have been renamed, deleted or put out of reach of this account, and quietly landing home beats greeting the user with an error on an empty pane. The probe costs one extra listing, but only once per connect.

      public void showDisconnected(String message)
      Puts the pane into a "not connected" state: clears the current listing and shows message as both the table placeholder and the status line. Used by the DualPaneBrowser so the remote pane reads "not connected" before a server connection rather than appearing empty.

    • batchRenameSelected

      public void batchRenameSelected()
      Opens the BatchRenameDialog for the current multi-selection and applies the resulting renames sequentially in the background. Only rows whose name actually changed are renamed; the dialog already blocks committing a plan with colliding targets. Falls back to single-file renameSelected() semantics when the user selects just one item and prefers a plain rename.

    • duplicateSelected

      public void duplicateSelected()
      Duplicates each selected entry in place under an auto-suffixed, non-colliding name (report.txt → report copy.txt, then report copy 2.txt, …). Names are reserved across the batch so duplicating several files at once never collides, and the running set is seeded from the current listing. Runs the copies sequentially off the FX thread.
